inference_dc.category: metro colocation / AI-cloud site (not a gigawatt training campus, not a micro edge PoP)
inference_dc.basis: Default 20 MW = CoreWeave fleet average (19.8 MW/site, YE2025), inside IEA 'conventional DC 10-25 MW'. Low 10 MW = IEA conventional lower bound (~ Digital Realty fleet average 9.4 MW). High 100 MW = IEA hyperscale AI-focused DC. g_default 0.30 = IEA Base Case growth of accelerated-server electricity 2024-2030 (fleet-level, not per-site); alternative 0.15 = IEA total DC electricity growth 2024-2030.

g_sources.source: IEA Energy and AI 2025 ch.2 p.63

g_sources.scope: global data centre electricity, 2024-2030 Base Case
g_sources.source: IEA Energy and AI 2025 ch.2 p.63

points.name: IEA 'conventional data centre'
points.arithmetic: IEA text: 'a conventional data centre may be around 10-25 MW'; Fig 1.12 note uses 25 MW as the conventional reference. Range 10-25 MW.
points.source: IEA, Energy and AI (Apr 2025), ch.1 p.38

points.name: IEA 'hyperscale, AI-focused data centre'
points.arithmetic: IEA text: 'A hyperscale, AI-focused data centre can have a capacity of 100 MW or more'; Fig 1.12 uses 100 MW.
points.source: IEA, Energy and AI (Apr 2025), ch.1 p.38

points.name: Digital Realty portfolio average
points.scope: colocation / wholesale DC, fleet average per facility
points.arithmetic: ~2.9 GW in-place IT capacity / 310 data centers (incl. 89 in JVs) = 2900/310 = 9.4 MW per facility

points.name: Digital Realty / Blackstone hyperscale JV
points.scope: planned hyperscale buildings (Frankfurt, Paris, N. Virginia)
points.arithmetic: ~500 MW potential IT load / 10 planned data centers = 50 MW per building

points.name: CoreWeave fleet average (AI cloud, mixed training+inference)
points.scope: GPU cloud DC, average per site
points.arithmetic: >850 MW active power / 43 data centers at YE2025 = 19.8 MW per site (lower bound since '>850')
points.source: CoreWeave blog 'A Defining Year for The Essential Cloud for AI'

points.name: Digital Realty Jakarta JV site
points.arithmetic: 'two buildings in Jakarta ... can support up to approximately 32 megawatts of IT load'

ai_lab.category: large AI-lab office campus (research/eval offices; excludes training compute)
ai_lab.basis: MW = floor area x CBECS 2018 office electricity intensity (13.6 kWh/sqft/yr mean) / 1000 / 8760. Default 1.5 MW = ~1M sqft SF campus (Anthropic, OpenAI 2026). Low 0.3 MW = single ~180-230k sqft building (DeepMind S2, Anthropic 500 Howard). High 1.9 MW = 1M sqft at 16.7 kWh/sqft (CBECS 10+ floor buildings). p is already average facility draw, so use u=1, PUE=1 in E = p x 8760 x u x PUE. Cross-check: Google offices 7.39 MWh/employee/yr (0.84 kW each) -> 1.5 MW ~ 1,780 employee-equivalents. g_default 0.35 = OpenAI SF floor-area CAGR (1,000,000/486,600)^(1/2.4)-1 (Oct 2023 -> Mar 2026); Anthropic implies (1,000,000/230,000)^(1/3)-1 = 0.63. Hypergrowth, not a long-run rate.
ai_lab.on_prem_note: No disclosed on-prem GPU clusters at AI-lab offices found; left null.

points.name: CBECS 2018 office electricity intensity
points.arithmetic: Office mean 13.6 kWh/sqft/yr (median 10.1, 75th pct 15.7); buildings with 10+ floors mean 16.7; office per worker 6.9 MWh/yr. 1,000,000 sqft x 13.6 = 13.6 GWh/yr / 8760 h = 1.55 MW avg

points.name: Alphabet offices & other facilities (all Google offices globally)
points.arithmetic: 1,354,300 MWh / 8760 = 154.6 MW avg (4.2% of 32,179,900 MWh total). Per employee: 1,354,300 / 183,323 = 7.39 MWh/yr = 0.84 kW avg (cf. CBECS office 6.9 MWh/worker)
points.source: Google 2025 Environmental Report p.114; Alphabet 10-K FY2024 (183,323 employees)

points.name: Anthropic SF office footprint (~1M sqft)
points.scope: AI lab HQ campus, SoMa SF
points.arithmetic: ~1,000,000 sqft (500 Howard 230k + 300 Howard 420k + 342 Howard 60k + 400 Howard 100k + 405 Howard ~70k = 880k; press: 'roughly 1 million') x 13.6 kWh/sqft = 13.6 GWh/yr / 8760 = 1.55 MW (at 16.7 kWh/sqft: 1.91 MW)

points.name: OpenAI Mission Bay (1455 + 1515 Third St)
points.source: SF Standard / SF Chronicle, Oct 2023; CBECS 2018

points.name: OpenAI SF total footprint (>1M sqft)
points.arithmetic: >1,000,000 sqft x 13.6 kWh/sqft = 13.6 GWh/yr / 8760 = 1.55 MW (lower bound on area)

points.name: Google DeepMind S2 building, King's Cross
points.scope: single AI lab office building, London
points.arithmetic: 180,000 sqft (11 floors) x 13.6 kWh/sqft (US CBECS; UK offices may differ) = 2.448 GWh/yr / 8760 = 0.279 MW
points.source: SES Engineering case study; Forbes 2019-03-08; CBECS 2018

caveats: Inference-specific per-site MW is rarely disclosed; CoreWeave and Digital Realty averages mix training, inference and general colocation.
No sourced MW for small edge/PoP sites (e.g. Cloudflare) was found; p_low is the IEA conventional-DC lower bound, not an edge PoP (which would be far below 1 MW).
CoreWeave 'active power' is energized contracted critical power, not metered draw; apply utilization u separately.
IEA 10-25 MW / 100 MW figures are illustrative typical sizes, not a survey distribution; Uptime 2024 survey report contains no facility-size MW distribution.
CBECS intensity is a US average office; AI labs with dense workstations, GPU dev boxes and 24/7 use likely exceed it. UK/EU offices may be lower.
AI-lab floor areas are press-reported lease totals (phased occupancy), not occupied conditioned area.
Google office electricity (1,354,300 MWh) includes 'other facilities', and Alphabet estimates some sites from square footage.
Web search budget was exhausted mid-task; Equinix per-site MW, Lambda/Nscale/Crusoe inference sites, and Microsoft/Meta office electricity splits were not captured.
